plan.topic: Backed up on Foundayo (orforglipron)? Constipation on the US label's common list, and gentle fluid and fibre habits
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Foundayo, the orforglipron pill, and feeling backed up? Constipation is a common, listed side effect.' Card: 'Constipation (adverse reaction): 24% on Foundayo 17.2 mg vs 9% on placebo, pooled Trials 1 and 2: adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes.' Untagged tips: build fibre up gradually with fluids, unless you've been told to limit fluids, and take a gentle walk. Ask a pharmacist before any laxative, with no product names. Untagged: if constipation is severe or keeps getting worse, contact your prescriber. Then the Foundayo emergency card with the full guide wording ('severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting … right away'), the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line.
plan.why: Pairs a searched approved-drug name with a felt symptom, the format behind Foundayo nausea (857) and food rules (1,063). It hasn't been covered, and it feeds the new Foundayo long video, which has a 71% average view. | fact-check: Checked. The Foundayo label prints constipation in the pooled placebo-controlled ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 table: 20% (5.5 mg), 27% (9 mg) and 24% (17.2 mg, the top label dose) vs 9% on placebo. Constipation is one of the label's most common adverse reactions. The rate goes on the card as 24% vs 9%. Never say 'up to 24%', because 9 mg was higher at 27%. Use 'adverse reactions', never 'side effects', on the rate card. The label's postmarketing section reports severe constipation, including fecal impaction. Add an untagged line pointing people with severe or worsening constipation to their prescriber, but don't present it as a common outcome. Fibre, fluid and walking tips are our own: no source tag, and never placed straight after a label claim. Keep the Foundayo pancreatitis wording 'with or without nausea or vomiting'. Cite 'Revised: 7/2026' only if that date is printed on the exact document linked. Watch-next target: ssb7Zcs3KSY.

package.title: Orforglipron (Foundayo): Backed Up? Not Rare #shorts
package.description:
Feeling backed up on Foundayo, the orforglipron pill, is not rare. Constipation is common. In the label's pooled trials, 24% on the top dose (17.2 mg) reported constipation vs 9% on placebo, over up to 72 weeks. Two gentle habits may help: build fibre up gradually with fluids (unless you've been told to limit fluids), and take a gentle walk. Thinking about a laxative? Ask a pharmacist first. If constipation is severe or keeps getting worse, contact your prescriber. Stop taking Foundayo and call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Orforglipron
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.hook_pattern: negation: "Feeling backed up on Foundayo, the orforglipron pill, is not rare." This is 11 words. It names the drug and the felt moment and is not a question. Sentence 2 opens on what it means for the viewer ("It is uncomfortable, but common") and gives the 24% vs 9% number by about 6 s. The label is credited only in the next sentence and on the card. Spoken word count, counted by hand: 155 (s1 11, s2 25, s3 26, s4 12, s5 27, s6 30, s7 24), with "twenty-four" counted as one word. The fact-checker logged s5 as 20 and s7 as 31. Those were the numbers before "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber." (7 words) moved from s7 to s5. The total is unchanged at 155, inside the standard arm of 135–160.

factcheck.summary: I checked the claims against Lilly's HTML label for Foundayo (uspl.lilly.com), which has both the Prescribing Information (PI) and the Medication Guide. Both pi.lilly.com PDFs load, but they couldn't be read as text. What the label confirms: Table 1 in PI Section 6.1 gives constipation at 24% on 17.2 mg vs 9% on placebo. The pooled data are Trials 1 and 2: 3,155 adults treated for up to 72 weeks, with and without type 2 diabetes. 17.2 mg is the top dose. The PI is printed "Revised: 7/2026". The Medication Guide lists constipation among the most common side effects, and its pancreatitis line includes "with or without nausea or vomiting". The script never ranks doses, which matters because 9 mg had a higher rate (27%). The fibre, fluid, walking and pharmacist tips have no source tag and carry the fluid-limit caveat, and nothing here is dosing or stop/switch advice. The hook pays off. The facts and safety are sound. Six small fixes are needed before render: the logged word count is off by one, the s2 stat card doesn't name the drug and dose, the s6 quote card isn't word for word, the safety lines are out of the required order, the S2 date label is wrong, and the s2 attribution should say how the trial populations split.

issues.problem: Counted by hand, s3 is 26 words, so the total is 155, not 156. That is still inside the 135–160 arm, but the log is wrong. Logging the wrong count is a known recurring fault.
issues.fix: Replace the count with: "Spoken word count, counted by hand: 155 (s1 11, s2 25, s3 26, s4 12, s5 20, s6 30, s7 31), with "twenty-four" counted as one word."

issues.problem: A muted viewer can't tell what this card measures. It doesn't name the outcome, the drug or the dose. Every stat card must name the drug and dose, both groups and the measure.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Constipation: 24% on Foundayo 17.2 mg vs 9% on placebo (up to 72 weeks)"

notes: Mascot is an outline-only/torso figure cropped at the frame edge, close to the 'mannequin hero' fault.
Caption card 'THE ORFORGLIPRON PILL,' ends on a comma.
Caption spells out 'TWENTY-FOUR' instead of using digits.
Card ends on the dangling word 'THE'.
Stat art correctly shows '24% vs 9%' but the caption underneath spells out 'NINE PERCENT' instead of using the digit to match the pill.
Caption card 'THAT'S FROM THE LABEL'S' ends on a possessive, a known banned ending.
Man is drawn as a floating head only, no neck or shoulders, cropped at the bottom of frame — the exact 'floating head' fault flagged repeatedly in QA.
Caption 'MAY HELP,' ends on a comma.
Shot list calls for a 'thinking woman' with a question, but the art shows only an abstract blue circle with a question mark — no human character present.
Shot list calls for a 'pharmacist' character, but the art shows an abstract blue circle and heart mascot with no pharmacist drawn.
Caption 'IS SEVERE,' ends on a comma, breaking an emergency-sign sentence.
Second card 'NOT PERSONAL ADVICE,' is the fixed safety card split at the comma instead of as one whole card.

Caption reads 'STOP TAKING FOUNDAYO' in isolation — this reverses the required don't-stop safety message and could be read as medical advice to discontinue medicine, a serious brand-safety and policy risk.

Emergency card wording is truncated/fragmented ('STOMACH AREA THAT WILL' / 'NAUSEA OR VOMITING.'), losing the guide's required full phrasing (healthcare provider, stomach area, with or without vomiting).
Card 'THAT EMERGENCY SIGN,' ends on a comma instead of a period.
